general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure 144 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 6/mm3 (92% lymphocytes; mildly raised). Protein 88 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 60 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.68). Gram stain: no organisms. Culture: no growth. Cytology: no malignant cells. Elevated protein with a mildly raised lymphocytic cell count; a single negative cytology does not exclude leptomeningeal malignancy. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.description: No vertebral or epidural metastatic deposit. Degenerative disc changes at L4-L5 without canal stenosis.
Smooth, thin enhancement of the cauda equina nerve roots, ventral roots more than dorsal. No nodular or sheet-like leptomeningeal enhancement.

output.impression: 1. Smooth enhancement of the cauda equina nerve roots, ventral more than dorsal, without nodularity. 2. No leptomeningeal nodules, epidural or vertebral metastasis. 3. Normal spinal cord signal; no cord or cauda equina compression. Clinical correlation recommended.

Myasthenia_Antibodies.clinical_significance: AChR antibodies are found in most patients with generalised myasthenia gravis, including most checkpoint inhibitor-related cases; a negative result does not exclude it. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Bedside respiratory function at 6 h: FVC 1.8 L (60% predicted; 25 mL/kg at 72 kg) L. MIP -28 cmH2O L. MEP 44 cmH2O L. Change: FVC 2.0 L to 1.8 L and MIP -32 to -28 cmH2O over 6 h (10% fall in FVC). Cough weak.
24-hour continuous telemetry. Sinus rhythm 64-102 bpm. No pauses and no arrhythmia. Blood pressure 112/68 to 162/94 mmHg.

Paraneoplastic.clinical_significance: Onconeural antibodies are found in a subset of paraneoplastic neurological syndromes; a negative result does not exclude one. Clinical correlation recommended.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week; repetitive stimulation without decrement and no myopathic units here
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support GBS and, with repetitive stimulation and needle EMG, separate it from checkpoint inhibitor myasthenia and myositis [EAN_PNS_2023, Schneider_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Raised protein (88 mg/dL) with a mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (6 cells/mm3), compatible with checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS; negative cytology and normal glucose argue against leptomeningeal metastasis
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein, glucose and cytology
action_criteria.rationale: CSF supports the diagnosis; with active stage IVB cancer and cranial nerve involvement, cytology is needed to look for leptomeningeal metastasis. Cells of 5-50/mm3 are compatible with GBS but prompt an alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No cord signal change, cord compression, epidural or vertebral metastasis and no nodular leptomeningeal enhancement; smooth nerve root enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Contrast spine MRI for urinary retention at onset in a patient with metastatic cancer
action_criteria.rationale: Bladder dysfunction at onset is a red flag for a spinal cord or cauda equina lesion [EAN_PNS_2023, Leonhard_2019]; with stage IVB cancer, metastatic compression and leptomeningeal disease must be excluded.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; low albumin (3.3 g/dL) marks a higher risk of a severe course; CK only mildly raised (286 U/L) and troponin normal, so no evidence of overlapping checkpoint inhibitor myositis or myocarditis; no metabolic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose, CK and troponin
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics and give the baseline before IVIg [EAN_PNS_2023]; in checkpoint inhibitor neurotoxicity CK and troponin screen for overlapping myositis and myocarditis [Schneider_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR (and MuSK) antibodies negative; with no decrement on repetitive stimulation, no ptosis, ophthalmoparesis or fatigability, checkpoint inhibitor myasthenia is unlikely
action_criteria.label: Acetylcholine receptor antibodies for checkpoint inhibitor myasthenia gravis
action_criteria.rationale: Myasthenia gravis is a recognised checkpoint inhibitor toxicity that can cause bulbar and respiratory weakness and overlaps with GBS and myositis [Schneider_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: She has dyspnoea, dysphagia and facial weakness and is still progressing; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level monitoring and intubation [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus rhythm 64-102 bpm without pauses and blood pressure 112/68 to 162/94 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction (here urinary retention) is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sinus rhythm 94 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 448 ms) and no ST-T change: baseline QTc on lenvatinib and no conduction abnormality to suggest myocarditis
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and checkpoint inhibitor myocarditis and gives the QTc on lenvatinib [EAN_PNS_2023, Schneider_2021].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Pembrolizumab identified as the checkpoint inhibitor behind the neurological toxicity; lenvatinib relevant for QT, renal function before IVIg, bleeding with line placement and blood pressure on steroids; amlodipine and hypotension with plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Check the medication list for interactions with pembrolizumab, lenvatinib, amlodipine and alendronate before IVIg, plasma exchange and corticosteroids
action_criteria.rationale: The medication list holds the culprit drug and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor whose QT, renal, bleeding and blood-pressure effects change how IVIg, plasma exchange and steroids are given (ROUND_POLICY ruling 6).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Onconeural antibodies negative; the acute demyelinating course does not suggest a paraneoplastic neuropathy
action_criteria.label: Optional onconeural antibody panel (anti-Hu, anti-Yo, anti-CV2/CRMP5)
action_criteria.rationale: A paraneoplastic neuropathy is in the differential of a patient with active cancer, but its subacute sensory-predominant course does not fit; the panel does not change acute management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General guidance on checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS; not needed for the diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on the management of checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not rechallenge with pembrolizumab or another checkpoint inhibitor after checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS [Schneider_2021].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function (lenvatinib can cause proteinuria and renal impairment).
Do not use succinylcholine if she needs intubation (risk of hyperkalaemia after denervation).
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level monitoring now: FVC 60% predicted and falling (2.0 to 1.8 L in 6 h), MIP -28 cmH2O, weak cough with dysphagia and bilateral facial weakness. Repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 2-4 hours and plan elective intubation if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.4 L at 72 kg), MIP or MEP keep worsening, bulbar function, cough or secretions worsen, or respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia appear [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].
Stop pembrolizumab permanently and hold lenvatinib while she is acutely ill, and agree the cancer plan with oncology [Schneider_2021, Haanen_2022].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 29 g/day at 72 kg) or plasma exchange (5 sessions), together with IV methylprednisolone (2-4 mg/kg/day, or a 1 g/day pulse for 5 days in severe disease) followed by a slow taper, as advised for checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS; monitor glucose and blood pressure on steroids [Schneider_2021, Haanen_2022].
Keep nil by mouth until a bedside swallow assessment is done (dysphagia, facial weakness); feed by nasogastric tube if the swallow is unsafe.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses; keep the urinary catheter for autonomic retention.

Screen for overlapping checkpoint inhibitor toxicities: repeat CK, troponin and ECG during the first days of treatment, and repeat thyroid function for the raised TSH with normal free T4 [Schneider_2021].
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin): active cancer and inability to walk [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated here: troponin and the ECG are normal and there is no haemodynamic instability; repeat troponin is the myocarditis screen.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome related to an immune checkpoint inhibitor (pembrolizumab)

differential.key_features: Can cause bulbar and respiratory weakness and overlap with GBS, but there is no ptosis, ophthalmoparesis or fatigable weakness, the reflexes are depressed with distal sensory loss, repetitive stimulation shows no decrement, AChR and MuSK antibodies are negative and the NCS is demyelinating.

Myalgias and CK 286 U/L raise it, but CK is under 2 times the upper limit, troponin is normal, needle EMG shows no myopathic units, and reflex loss, sensory symptoms and demyelinating conduction are not myopathic. CK and troponin are repeated.

Active stage IVB cancer with cranial nerve involvement; CSF glucose normal, cytology negative and spine MRI shows smooth root enhancement without nodularity. One negative cytology does not exclude it: repeat CSF cytology if she does not respond.

differential.diagnosis: Metastatic spinal cord or cauda equina compression
differential.key_features: Urinary retention in a patient with metastatic cancer, but no back pain, no sensory level, flexor plantars, facial and arm involvement, and no epidural or vertebral disease on spine MRI.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.
Usually subacute and sensory-predominant (sensory neuronopathy); the acute motor-predominant demyelinating course after pembrolizumab does not fit.
Prior paclitaxel can explain reduced sensory potentials, but not acute limb, facial and bulbar weakness, demyelinating motor conduction or raised CSF protein.

key_clinical_evidence: Ascending limb weakness with depressed reflexes, bilateral facial weakness and dysphagia beginning days after a second pembrolizumab cycle, with raised CSF protein (88 mg/dL, 6 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS: GBS related to the checkpoint inhibitor.

For checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS, ASCO and ESMO guidance gives IVIg or plasma exchange with corticosteroids and stops the checkpoint inhibitor permanently [Schneider_2021, Haanen_2022]; EAN/PNS advice against corticosteroids is written for GBS in general [EAN_PNS_2023], and the oncology guidance governs this case.
Checkpoint inhibitor neurotoxicity can overlap with myasthenia, myositis and myocarditis: repetitive stimulation, AChR antibodies, CK, troponin and the ECG screen for them [Schneider_2021].

Urinary retention at onset is a red flag; in metastatic cancer the contrast spine MRI and CSF cytology exclude compression and leptomeningeal disease before the retention is attributed to autonomic GBS [EAN_PNS_2023].
A mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (5-50 cells/mm3) is compatible with GBS but calls for exclusion of an alternative, here leptomeningeal metastasis [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Onset days after the second pembrolizumab cycle with an acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy points to the checkpoint inhibitor; negative CSF cytology, normal CSF glucose and a spine MRI without metastatic or nodular leptomeningeal disease make the cancer an unlikely direct cause.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors on a paraneoplastic neuropathy, leptomeningeal metastasis or metastatic compression rather than checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Subclinical thyroid dysfunction, common with pembrolizumab and with lenvatinib, does not cause acute areflexic weakness with facial and bulbar involvement, raised CSF protein and demyelinating conduction; it is followed with repeat thyroid function.
red_herrings.data_point: TSH 14.0 mIU/L with normal free T4
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests that hypothyroidism explains the weakness, myalgias and fatigue.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: No back pain, sensory level or upper motor neuron signs, and the spine MRI shows no compression or cord lesion; autonomic involvement in GBS explains the retention.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Bladder dysfunction at onset is a red flag for a spinal cord or cauda equina lesion.

sequence_constraints.reason: Renal function, electrolytes and calcium are needed to judge the lenvatinib interactions before IVIg and plasma exchange.

general.formulary_status: IVIg, methylprednisolone and albumin for plasma exchange: formulary
interactions: Lenvatinib: QT interval prolongation is a labelled adverse effect; keep potassium, magnesium and calcium normal and monitor the ECG when other QT-prolonging drugs are added (relative caution).
Lenvatinib: proteinuria and renal impairment are labelled adverse effects; check creatinine and urine protein before IVIg, which can cause acute kidney injury (relative caution).
Lenvatinib: haemorrhagic events are a labelled adverse effect; relative caution with central venous catheter placement for plasma exchange and with lumbar puncture.
Lenvatinib: hypertension is a labelled adverse effect; corticosteroids add to blood pressure and cause hyperglycaemia (monitor blood pressure and glucose).
Amlodipine: additive hypotension with the fluid shifts of plasma exchange (relative caution).
Plasma exchange with citrate anticoagulation lowers ionised calcium; lenvatinib can also cause hypocalcaemia (monitor calcium). Alendronate has no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange.
general.proposed: IVIg, plasma exchange or IV methylprednisolone with the current medication list
general.summary: Category-level review of pembrolizumab, lenvatinib, amlodipine and alendronate against IVIg, plasma exchange and IV methylprednisolone.
warnings: Pembrolizumab: immune checkpoint inhibitor. Immune-related adverse events can involve peripheral nerve, neuromuscular junction, muscle, myocardium, thyroid and skin, and the effect persists for weeks after the last dose.

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 94. Normal intervals (QTc 448 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL (low). Albumin 3.3 g/dL (low). CK 286 U/L (elevated). CRP 42.8 mg/L (elevated). TSH 14.0 mIU/L (elevated) with normal free T4. CA-125 312 U/mL (elevated). Remaining values within reference ranges.

general.query: management of Guillain-Barre syndrome related to immune checkpoint inhibitors

results.finding: For Guillain-Barre syndrome during immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, ASCO guidance advises permanent discontinuation of the checkpoint inhibitor, admission with rapid access to intensive care, IVIg or plasma exchange, and a trial of corticosteroids, which it considers reasonable in this setting although not in idiopathic GBS.
ESMO guidance for neurological immune-related adverse events advises stopping the checkpoint inhibitor and treating GBS with IVIg or plasma exchange, with corticosteroids considered in addition.
For GBS in general, oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended; IVIg and plasma exchange are equally effective.

general.summary: Oncology irAE guidance treats checkpoint inhibitor-related GBS with IVIg or plasma exchange plus corticosteroids and permanent withdrawal of the checkpoint inhibitor [Schneider_2021, Haanen_2022]; general GBS guidance advises against corticosteroids [EAN_PNS_2023].

findings.nerve: Repetitive nerve stimulation at 3 Hz (median-abductor pollicis brevis, spinal accessory-trapezius)

findings.finding: Tibialis anterior, vastus lateralis, deltoid and first dorsal interosseous bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units; no myopathic units; no fibrillation potentials or positive sharp waves

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in bilateral peroneal and median motor nerves, with reduced CMAP amplitudes. 2. Absent F-waves (peroneal) and prolonged F-wave latencies (median); absent H-reflexes. 3. Absent sural and reduced median sensory nerve action potentials. 4. No decrement on 3 Hz repetitive nerve stimulation. 5. Reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units without myopathic units or denervation on needle EMG. Pattern consistent with a demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.pattern: Demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy with reduced distal motor amplitudes

metadata.difficulty_description: Pembrolizumab-related GBS in a patient with active uterine cancer: paraneoplastic neuropathy, leptomeningeal metastasis, checkpoint inhibitor myasthenia and myositis, and thyroid dysfunction compete with the diagnosis.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 6 required and 3 recommended actions, 3 red herrings; checkpoint inhibitor overlap syndromes, a bladder red flag and the steroid exception to the general GBS guideline.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive weakness, shortness of breath and inability to walk 7 days after a second pembrolizumab cycle in a patient with advanced uterine cancer.

past_medical_history: Uterine adenocarcinoma, stage IVB, on pembrolizumab and lenvatinib (previously carboplatin-paclitaxel)

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. O. is a 70-year-old woman with stage IVB uterine adenocarcinoma who presents with progressive weakness 7 days after her second cycle of pembrolizumab, which she receives with daily lenvatinib. Her disease progressed after an initial partial radiographic response to carboplatin-paclitaxel, and she was switched to pembrolizumab and lenvatinib about 4 weeks ago. Over the days after the second infusion she developed tingling and numbness of the hands and feet, diffuse myalgias and worsening fatigue, then weakness of the legs, and she can no longer walk without support from two people. She reports shortness of breath, painful swallowing and difficulty swallowing solids. A maculopapular rash appeared on her trunk. Today she was unable to void and required urinary catheterization. She has had no back pain, fever or double vision.

neurological_exam.additional: Urinary retention requiring catheterization. Diffuse maculopapular rash on the trunk.
neurological_exam.coordination: Mild limb ataxia bilaterally. Bilateral hand tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Dysphagia with difficulty swallowing solids. Mild bilateral facial weakness. No ptosis. Eye movements full, no ophthalmoplegia. Pupils equal and reactive.
neurological_exam.gait: Unable to walk independently; requires bilateral support.
neurological_exam.motor: Lower limbs: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 bilaterally. Upper limbs 4/5 bilaterally. No fatigable weakness on repeated testing.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Hyporeflexia bilaterally: patellar 1+, Achilles trace, upper limb reflexes trace. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal paraesthesias and numbness in a glove-and-stocking distribution. No sensory level.
